title: Eye anatomy: layers, lens and visual pathway
description: Sagittal section: an optical instrument that focuses light onto a neural film.

questions.question: How does the eye focus light on the retina?
questions.answer: The cornea provides much of the eye's focusing power, while the lens changes shape for near and far vision. Light is converted into neural signals by retinal photoreceptors.

questions.question: What is the difference between the retina and the optic nerve?
questions.answer: The retina is the light-sensitive neural tissue lining the back of the eye. Its ganglion-cell axons bundle together to form the optic nerve.

questions.question: What is the cornea?
questions.answer: Transparent, avascular, five-layered dome at the front of the eye. Provides about two-thirds of the eye's refractive power. Function: Bends and transmits light; its endothelium pumps water out to stay clear.

questions.question: Where is the retina located?
questions.answer: Ten-layered neural film: photoreceptors outermost (light must pass through the inner layers first), then bipolar and ganglion cells. Function: Transduces light into nerve impulses.

questions.question: What is the function of the macula & fovea?
questions.answer: Function: High-acuity central vision for reading and faces. A 5.5 mm yellow-pigmented area at the posterior pole; its centre, the fovea, contains cones only and no vessels.
